description: PIV commands answered by OpenFIPS201 on a blank card, replayed through the Java Card engine.
note: These run as one ordered session against one freshly installed card. The VERIFY cases depend on the retry counter left by the case before them, so the order is part of the fixture.

exchanges.description: SELECT the PIV application by its full applet AID
exchanges.source: NIST SD33 card 02 capture, contact interface
exchanges.why: The applet registered this AID during install and its own select method agreed to become current.

exchanges.description: GET DATA for the Discovery Object
exchanges.source: NIST SD33 card 02 capture, contact interface
exchanges.why: SP 800-73-4 part 2. A card holding no such object answers referenced data not found. The captured card answered 9000 because it was personalised.

exchanges.description: GET DATA for the Card Capability Container
GET DATA for the Card Holder Unique Identifier
GET DATA for the PIV Authentication Certificate
GET DATA for the Secure Messaging Certificate Signer
exchanges.source: NIST SD33 card 02 capture, contact interface
exchanges.why: Absent on a blank card. The captured card answered 9000.

exchanges.description: GET DATA naming an object the card does not define
exchanges.why: An unknown object identifier is still a well formed request for something absent.

exchanges.description: GET DATA whose data field is not a 5C tag list
exchanges.why: The data field must be a 5C tag list, so a different tag is an incorrect parameter in the data field. This case separates a malformed request from an absent object.

exchanges.description: VERIFY the PIV application PIN with a wrong value
exchanges.source: SP 800-73-4 part 2 section 3.2.1, padded to eight bytes
exchanges.why: SELECT processing applies Config.DEFAULT_PIN_RETRIES_CONTACT = 6 in the pinned OpenFIPS201 source. Five remain after one failure.

exchanges.description: VERIFY the PIV application PIN with a second wrong value
exchanges.source: SP 800-73-4 part 2 section 3.2.1, padded to eight bytes
exchanges.why: The counter goes down again and stays down, which is the applet's own OwnerPIN state surviving from one command to the next.

exchanges.description: VERIFY naming a key reference the card does not hold
exchanges.why: Referenced data or reference data not found, for a key reference outside the set the applet defines.

exchanges.description: A command the applet does not implement
exchanges.why: Instruction not supported or invalid, which proves the applet reached its own dispatch rather than the engine failing first.
